Their largest lead reached 38 points in the fourth quarter and the Lakers never led at any point in the contest.
Yaxel Lendeborg paced the team in scoring with 17 points, followed by Stephen Curry (16) and Brandin Podziemski (16).
FIRST QUARTER FINISHING The Dubs wasted no time in their home court debut, going on a 11-2 scoring run to start the first quarter that quickly evolved into a double digit lead.
They scored 45 points in the frame with their advantage reaching a high of 20 points at one point.
The high-scoring quarter was highlighted by a Draymond Green buzzer beater 3-pointer and a Stephen Curry four-point play as he earned the hoop and harm from beyond the arc.
Curry led the scoring across both teams in the first, contributing 11 points in eight minutes.
The sequence started with a tough and-1 play and followed by a penetrating drive to the rim off a Draymond Green dime to secure another bucket.

posts.title: Utah Jazz Fall in Preseason Rematch Against Nuggets: Three Takeaways

posts.summary: Utah Jazz basketball is back at the Delta Center.
facts: The Jazz continued their pregame slate Tuesday night with a rematch against the Denver Nuggets, as fans got an in-person glimpse of the 2026-27 squad.
After defeating Denver Sunday night in Boulder, CO, the Jazz fell 117-106 at home, with a few cold shooting spells and an inability to avoid fouls hurting Utah’s efforts.
Rookie Darryn Peterson thrived to the tune of 23 points on 10-of-18 shooting to lead all scorers.
On the offensive end, good ball movement (nine assists on 13 made shots) and a hot stretch from beyond the arc (5-of-9) helped Utah put up 31 points over the first 12 minutes of action.
A cold spell offensively from the Jazz helped the Nuggets tie the game at 40.
Utah began the second frame 3-of-10 from the field before Peterson found a rhythm to help steady the offense.
The rookie finished the first half with 12 and was the only Jazzman in double figures.
Unfortunately for the Jazz, their shooting struggles continued and even came from the free-throw line (5-of-11 in the frame), which helped Denver take a 65-59 lead into the halftime break.

posts.summary: After a summer full of anticipation, Utah Jazz basketball made its return Sunday night.
facts: After a summer full of anticipation, Utah Jazz basketball made its return Sunday night.
Although it was only a preseason matchup against the Denver Nuggets, Jazz fans finally got to see the 2026-27 squad in action.
Utah fought through multiple cold spells offensively to gain control and pull out a 109-97 win to open the preseason slate of games.
The long ball was a key weapon for the Jazz (15 made threes), while an edge on the boards (63-55) also helped fuel the victory.
The Jazz closed the opening frame on a 19-6 run, fueled by good ball movement (11 assists in the quarter) and hot shooting (52 percent from the field and five made 3-pointers).
It was a similar story in the second quarter, as Utah shot 1-of-10 from the field to begin the frame before using regular trips to the free-throw line to find more of a rhythm on the offensive end.
Lauri Markkanen totaled 17 points in the first half, with Jaren Jackson Jr. (11 points) and Keyonte George (10 points) following The Finnisher’s lead.
On the defensive end, the Jazz forced six turnovers and limited Denver to 44 percent shooting from the field, which helped push the visitors in front 63-52.
